newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALY'S RAVANELLI RULED OUT BY INJURY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALY'S RAVANELLI RULED OUT BY INJURY.

text.p: Injured striker Fabrizio Ravanelli will miss Italy's World Cup qualifiers against Moldova in Trieste on Saturday and away against Poland on April 2.
The Middlesbrough player has been suffering muscular problems and was ruled out after tests at the Italian training ground near Florence.
Team officials said Ravanelli would need three days of complete rest and could not be fit in time.
He will remain with his Italy team mates until Thursday and would then be free to return to England.
"There's no chance of an immediate recovery," said a team doctor. "The injured part has still not healed."
Ravanelli said he was particularly disappointed as he was going through a patch of good form and wanted to break his personal goalscoring record of 31 goals in a season.
The striker has scored 29 so far in the English premier league, cup competitions and international matches.
"I also want to be the first Italian to win an English cup," Ravanelli told reporters.
"We're in the League Cup final and F.A. Cup semifinal. We can do it. Just as Middlesbrough can save itself in the league. I'll think about everything else at the end of the season."
Middlesbrough lifted themselves out of the relegation zone at the weekend with a 1-0 win against Chelsea.

In Ravanelli's absence, Italy coach Cesare Maldini is expected to field Juventus's Christian Vieri, who is recovering from an ankle problem, up front in a team already without Lazio striker Pier Luigi Casiraghi.
Following their 1-0 win against England at Wembley last month, Italy are joint top of group two with England on nine points but with a game in hand.
